question: What does a sudden draft drop indicate?
system_answer: Troubleshooting Guide Symptom: sudden draft drop A sudden draft drop indicates loss of suction. Reading the draft signals A sudden drop in draft magnitude, meaning the draft moving toward zero, indicates loss of induced-draft fan capacity, a closing damper, or a trip of the fan. [Troubleshooting_Guide.pdf p.1], [Cyclone_Operating_Manual.pdf p.1]

question: What causes the cone draft to diverge from the outlet draft?
system_answer: Cone draft behaviour When the cone draft becomes less negative than the outlet draft by more than 25 mbar, material build-up or a blockage in the cone or dip-leg is likely. Inlet draft is normally between -150 and -250 mbar; the cone draft is normally 20 to 40 mbar more negative than the outlet draft. [Cyclone_Operating_Manual.pdf p.2], [Cyclone_Operating_Manual.pdf p.1]

question: Why is the first hour after restart unstable?
system_answer: The first hour after restart is an unstable period: the inlet temperature ramps upward at more than 25 C per hour and temperature variance is high. Raise an information alert when the one hour standard deviation of inlet temperature exceeds 45 C outside the first hour after restart. [Startup_and_Shutdown_SOP.pdf p.1], [Alarm_and_Monitoring_Guide.pdf p.1]

question: Material temperature stuck at 40 while gas temperatures are normal, what is wrong?
system_answer: A material temperature reading that is flat at about 40 C while gas temperatures are normal indicates an instrument fault, not a process upset. Symptom: frozen sensor value A sensor that stays at exactly the same value while others move is stuck or stale. [Cyclone_Operating_Manual.pdf p.2], [Troubleshooting_Guide.pdf p.2]

question: How would I notice cold air leaking into the system?
system_answer: With a draft that becomes more negative the likely cause is cold false air entering the system. A draft that becomes more negative than normal with falling gas temperature indicates false air ingress, for example an open inspection door or a leaking expansion joint. [Troubleshooting_Guide.pdf p.1], [Cyclone_Operating_Manual.pdf p.1]
